title: DEI-based recruitment for the STEM is great for the economy and great for increasing job opportunities for the US public
content: The many DEI (diversity, equality, and inclusion) initiatives and programs at the US federal and state levels have likely played an important role in increasing recruitment to STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) careers—and not at the expense of White male candidates. It is actually and factually difficult to conduct research in the United States without foreign graduate students. The various DEI programs and their emphasis in federal grant proposals was a way to increase American contributions to the STEM fields by recruiting from underrepresented groups with US citizenship or on the pathway to citizenship. Many foreign graduate students stay in the United States to pursue academic and other careers, or they return to their countries and, through their contributions, strengthen democratic and free-market ideals. These are certainly worthy investments by the US taxpayer. The emphasis of the Trump administration is to increase opportunities for US citizens; fair enough. But if there is a shortage of available talent in the United States, why not try to recruit from those groups that would like to participate in the STEM but have not because of institutional barriers? It is the low-hanging fruit to both strengthening US capacity and increasing the opportunities available to the US public. The Trump administration, including the president and his acolytes, is allowing the culture wars to interfere with economic progress for all Americans.
